inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation $214M; plus ~$50M ESTIMATED cash tax withheld on net-share settlement (XBRL tag PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation discontinued after FY2023 when it was $32M on $122M SBC; scaled to FY2026 SBC). TJX publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-08-01), 1,117M. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks ($2.52B FY2026, $1.42B in H1 FY2027, $2.50-2.75B planned FY2027) more than fund it, so the flat count is paid for in cash, and the excess retirement is treated as a use of owner FCF, not extra value.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.85 for a defensive-leaning discretionary retailer -> cost of equity ~8.5%. Debt is $2.87B against ~$149B market cap and the company is net cash, so WACC ~= cost of equity: 8.5%, the same in every scenario (risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not the rate).
inputs.lease_treatment: Single treatment: operating-lease rent (FY2026 operating lease cost $2,196M) sits inside SG&A under ASC 842, so it is already deducted in EBITDA; the $10.6B operating-lease liability is therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Never both.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route), 10-year horizon. TJX is a profitable US operating retailer with real free cash flow; no bank/REIT/holdco features, no prior valuation or memory entry. ANCHORS: price Yahoo 2026-10-01 close; cash $6,004M and debt $2,871M ($1,871M non-current + $1,000M current notes) from Q2 FY2027 10-Q balance sheet dated 2026-08-01; net cash $3,133M. FY0 = FY2026 (ended 2026-01-31, revenue $60,372M). EBITDA basis: FY2026 pretax $7,299M less net interest income $116M ($195M income - $79M expense) = EBIT $7,183M (11.9%); + D&A $1,247M + SBC $214M = adj. EBITDA (pre-SBC, ex-interest, post-rent) $8,644M = 14.3% of revenue. FY2027 guidance (Q2 call 2026-08-19): pretax margin 12.3-12.4% (raised), EPS $5.31-5.36, comps 2-3%, net sales +4-5%, though H1 FY2027 revenue actually ran +7.2% ($29,503M vs $27,512M). Year-1 owner-FCF margin check: ~7.5% vs FY2026 actual owner FCF $4,458M / $60,372M = 7.4% - no one-off is carried forward. Interest income ($195M) deducted from the FCF base because net cash is added in the bridge; the engine's EBITDA basis excludes it. CSV quarterly labels run one quarter late (CSV 'Q3 2027' = fiscal Q2 FY2027, 'H2-2027' = H1 FY2027) - a data-label issue, read accordingly. Repurchaser: flat share count is funded.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (17.0%) diverges >30% from revenue 3yr CAGR (6.5%). Book value is not a usable growth proxy here: TJX returns essentially all FCF via buybacks and dividends, so equity growth reflects margin recovery and retained-vs-returned mix, not reinvestment. Revenue CAGR from FY2023 is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: 5-year windows start at FY2021 (COVID store closures: revenue $32.1B, EPS $0.08), so revenue 5yr 13.4% is a rebound artefact and EPS 5yr is meaningless (null). Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - est. equity-award taxes - interest income): FY2021 ~$3,893M (working-capital release), FY2023 ~$2,397M, FY2026 ~$4,458M; 3yr 23% reflects margin recovery from the FY2022-23 freight/inventory trough, not a sustainable rate. SBC (~0.35% of revenue) is small and growing roughly in line with revenue, so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs barely differ.

base.narrative: FY2027 lands near the raised guide (pretax ~12.3%, sales +5.5%); store growth steps up to ~4%/yr from FY2028 with 2-3% comps, then fades toward 3% as the 7,500-store target matures. EBIT margin creeps from 11.9% to ~12.4% on merchandise margin and leverage, partly spent on marketing and wages.

scenario_narratives.base: The off-price share-gain story continues at its historical pace: comps 2-3%, ~4% annual store growth from FY2028 toward the raised 7,500-store target, HomeGoods and TK Maxx International growing slightly faster than Marmaxx. Tariff costs are absorbed through opportunistic buying and pricing; the Q2 FY2027 Marmaxx merchandise-mix miss is a one-quarter execution slip. Increased marketing spend and wage inflation consume most of the merchandise-margin and occupancy leverage, so EBIT margin rises only ~50bp over a decade to ~12.4%. Capex runs ~3.6% of sales during the store acceleration, then eases.
scenario_narratives.bull: Department-store and full-price closures plus abundant vendor overstock (tariff-disrupted supply chains push more goods into off-price) let TJX run 3-4% comps on top of 4%+ store growth; Spain and other new markets work and HomeGoods/Homesense take home-decor share. Marketing investment converts into traffic, and merchandise margin plus scale leverage take EBIT margin to ~13.6% (pretax ~14%), above anything TJX has printed. Exit at 22x terminal owner FCF is consistent with the premium the market already pays for the franchise.
scenario_narratives.bear: A US consumer downturn hits discretionary apparel/home in FY2028 while tariffs and retaliatory measures raise landed costs; Ross and Burlington price more aggressively, Marmaxx execution errors recur, and vendor inventory discipline tightens off-price supply. Comps go flat-to-negative for a year, store growth is slowed to protect returns, and EBIT margin falls back to ~10.8% (FY2023-24 levels) and stays there as wage costs and the new marketing budget prove sticky. Off-price still trades customers down, so revenue does not shrink - the bear is a margin and multiple story (16x exit), not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): tariffs are flagged as a high-severity risk in the FY2026 10-K, Q2 FY2027 showed a self-inflicted Marmaxx slowdown, and FY2027 margins sit at a record high, so mean reversion is a live path; the balance sheet carries no solvency risk, which keeps it from going higher. Base 50%: guidance has been raised twice and the store-growth plan is concrete. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): the bull needs both faster store growth AND record margins with marketing spend paying back - two independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: TJX is a mature, high-return compounder whose value rests on durable off-price share gains and a ~12% EBIT margin, not on growth optionality. The valuation is an owner-FCF DCF at an 8.5% USD WACC: SBC fully expensed (immaterial at ~0.36% of sales), interest income on the cash pile stripped because net cash is added in the bridge, operating-lease rent kept inside EBITDA with lease liabilities excluded from net debt. Buybacks are value-neutral in the model; they are how TJX returns the owner FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin mean reversion from a record FY2027 pretax margin (12.3-12.4%) - every 100bp of EBITDA margin is roughly 8-9% of value
Tariff and trade-policy cost on merchandise margin (FY2026 10-K high-severity risk)
Store-growth acceleration to ~4%/yr toward 7,500 stores may cannibalise or earn lower returns in new markets (Spain)
Equity-award withholding taxes are estimated (~$50M) since the XBRL tag ended in FY2023 - immaterial to value
Terminal-value heavy: a 10-year horizon on a mature retailer means ~2/3 of EV sits in the terminal value
